facts.value: If yoshiegg.x14<=0 on invocation, call Fighter_UpdateModelScale, clear accessory4_cb and return without a local accessory-scale reset. Otherwise decrement x14 by one, compute m=(1-xC)+((x10-x14)/x10)*xC, multiply saved root x18 and accessory scale vectors componentwise by m, and write both JObj scales. Reaching zero through the decrement still performs scaling; cleanup waits for another invocation. No clamping or finite/nonzero-denominator validation guarantees monotonic growth, eventual completion or an exact final accessory baseline. Fractional countdowns may overshoot; NaN x14 bypasses the cleanup comparison under ordinary nontrapping floating-point semantics.
facts.rationale: Replaces progressively-larger behavior with exact guard order, arithmetic and boundaries.

evidence.why: Complete countdown guard, formula, two scale writes and self-removal.

facts.value: Entry conditionally applies airborne setup to a grounded victim, enters ftCo_MS_YoshiEgg, hides it, loads/scales/attaches its accessory, initializes the specialized hurt capsule, source-derived velocity/facing/damage behavior, grab state and interpolation inputs, and installs primary/secondary damage and accessory4 callbacks. Canonical initialization writes mv.ca.specialhi.vel.y=0 and yoshiegg.x14=mv.co.walk.fast_anim_frame; intended union aliases remain unresolved without compiled layout evidence. The scale callback can unregister before captivity ends and is suppressed by the inspected scheduler when x221F_b3 or x2219_b5 is set. Motion-state callback setup clears accessory4_cb and both damage slots.
facts.rationale: Removes unsupported until-expiry lifetime guarantees while preserving verified initialization and canonical field spellings.

evidence.why: Complete setup and canonical cross-union writes.
Callback slot clearing during motion-state setup.

facts.value: Each invocation subtracts ftYs_SpecialN_GetExtAttr28 from grab_timer, calls ftCommon_GrabMash with ftYs_SpecialN_GetExtAttr2C, stores its result in x4, and then tests grab_timer<=0. Expiration performs sound/effect, release velocity, airborne/model-scale and collision setup, calls ftCo_Fall_Enter_YoshiEgg and returns. That helper permits x2224_b2 and ftCo_800C5240 alternate routes before default Fall. Otherwise any nonzero x8, including a negative value, is decremented; a resulting nonpositive x8 with false x4 resets animation rate to 1 and x8 to zero. Independently, nonpositive x8 with true x4 reloads configured duration and rate. Zero x8 with no mash does nothing. No finite-value validation exists; under ordinary nontrapping semantics NaN timer fails the exit test and NaN x8 fails the nonpositive comparisons.
facts.rationale: Corrects positive-versus-nonzero guard, preserves update ordering and documents optional exit paths.

facts.value: The registered YoshiEgg IASA callback is empty: no parameter dereference, input check, timer mutation, call or transition occurs in this phase. The local Anim callback owns decay, mash processing and the timer-conditioned release sequence. This does not prove that timer expiry is the only external reason the fighter can leave YoshiEgg.
facts.rationale: Preserves invariant no-op behavior while removing an unsupported global exclusivity claim.

evidence.why: Local timer path and complete empty IASA definition.

facts.value: Entry reads the capturing fighter's accessory descriptor, facing, launch velocity, damage behavior, interpolation parameters and initial grab duration through Yoshi SpecialN accessors. The accessory's initial uniform scale and specialized hurt-capsule geometry instead come from the victim's co_attrs.xBC, and the root baseline is copied from the victim's JObj. Later callbacks consume victim state; recurring decay, mash feedback, release tuning and the damage-to-timer coefficient are read from global Yoshi extended attributes rather than the retained source pointer.
facts.rationale: Repairs the baseline's incorrect attribution of accessory scaling to Yoshi and distinguishes per-source inputs, victim baselines and global recurring tuning.

evidence.why: Per-object dat_attrs, descriptor, and global ext_attr accessor implementations.
